title: Ordered affine-space integration and the binary relative product
statement:
In the finite-coefficient conventions [def-pur-conventions], put $A=A_{E,n}$ and let $Y$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme. Write $p_m:X_m=\mathbf A^m_Y\to Y$, $m\geq1$, and $q_m:X_{m+1}\to X_m$ for the last-coordinate affine-line projection [def-sbc-affine-space], so $p_{m+1}=p_mq_m$. Put $T_m=A_{X_m}(m)[2m]$ using [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], $V_m=Rp_{m!}T_m$, $a=p_1$, $T=T_1$, and $U=Ra_!T$. Let $t_Y:U\to A_Y$ be exactly the normalized integration in [def-pur-affine-line-purity-comparison]. Let $\gamma_{p_m,A_Y}$ be the ordered comparison [def-pur-affine-space-comparison], and define its actual exceptional transpose by
$$I_m=\varepsilon_{p_m,A_Y}\circ Rp_{m!}(\gamma_{p_m,A_Y}):V_m\longrightarrow A_Y,$$
using the constructible exceptional adjunction [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] and the tensor-unit identification of the source. Assume that the $V_m$ are bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude, and that these affine-line integrations commute with base change: for every $v:Y'\to Y$ between separated finite-type $k$-schemes, $v^*t_Y=t_{Y'}\circ\operatorname{Ex}_!$ under the canonical Tate pullback identifications; make the same assumption over each such base $Y'$. Let
$$\kappa_{m,1}:V_{m+1}\xrightarrow{\sim}V_m\otimes_A^LU$$
be the specified relative compact-support product construction of [thm-sf-kunneth-relative] for $(p_m,T_m)$ and $(a,T)$, with $T_m\boxtimes T=T_{m+1}$ under canonical twist, shift and pullback identifications. Then the actual maps satisfy
$$I_1=t_Y,\qquad I_{m+1}=(I_m\otimes t_Y)\circ\kappa_{m,1}\quad(m\geq1),$$
where $A_Y\otimes_A^LA_Y\cong A_Y$ is understood. The assertion uses the canonical finite-coefficient exchanges, projection transformations and compact-support composition comparisons; it makes no coordinate-permutation assertion.

source.place: Proof Steps 3--4, as expanded in returned split Step 7: identifying the pasted ordered integration with (I_m tensor t) composed with the canonical binary product map

proof.text: Fix $m\geq1$. Write $p=p_m:X_m\to Y$, $q=q_m:X_{m+1}\to X_m$ and $r:X_{m+1}\to X_1$ for the first-$m$ and last-coordinate projections, respectively. Thus $pq=ar=p_{m+1}$ and $q$ is the base change of $a$ along $p$. The ordered definition [def-pur-affine-space-comparison] supplies these identifications and the twist identification $T_{m+1}=q^*T_m\otimes^L r^*T$. All sources and bases are separated finite type. Each $T_j$ is bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude: by [prop-weil-twist-preserves] its unshifted twist is locally free of rank one; shifting by $2j$ shifts its Tor interval. The assumption supplies this property for $V_j$, including $U=V_1$. Bounded constructible inputs have etale representatives by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]; [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude] gives the finite-Tor property of those representatives. Consequently [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula] applies to the four pairs $(q,r^*T,T_m)$, $(p,T_m,U)$, $(r,q^*T_m,T)$ and $(a,T,V_m)$. The exchanges for the two product squares are isomorphisms by [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale]. The intermediate exceptional input $Rp^!A_Y$ of the ordered recursion is in $D^b_{ctf}$ by [thm-sf-preservation-class](2). Only the constructible adjunction already specified in the ordered definition is used.

source.place: Integration paragraph: coordinate tower and applicability of the projection formulas

proof.text: For any affine-line projection $u:L\to B$, put $F_uK=u^*K\otimes^L A_L(1)[2]$ and write $b_{u,K}:Ru_!F_uK\to K$ for the defining transpose in [def-pur-affine-line-purity-comparison]. That definition gives $b_{u,K}=\rho_K(1_K\otimes t_B)\Pi^u_K$, where $\rho$ is the tensor-unit map and $\Pi^u_K$ is precisely its two-symmetry inverse projection formula. It is natural in $K$, by the naturality in [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula]. At $K=A_B$ the projection transformation is the tensor-unit identification: the proper factor has this normalization by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact], while the open tensor comparison in [def-exchange-projection] sends $x\otimes1$ to $x\otimes1$ and is the identity after the unit identifications. The two symmetries in $\Pi^u_{A_B}$ are also unit identifications. Hence $b_{u,A_B}=t_B$. The rank-one case of the recursion [def-pur-affine-space-comparison] is the specified line comparison (the rank-zero map and the composition with the identity are identities). The inverse Hom bijection takes that comparison back to $b_{a,A_Y}$. Therefore $I_1=t_Y$.

source.place: Integration paragraph: the normalized affine-line trace, the base of the recursion

proof.text:
Compute the actual transpose at the next stage. Abbreviate $\gamma_m=\gamma_{p,A_Y}:T_m\to Rp^!A_Y$ and $\alpha=\alpha_{p,q}:Rp_!Rq_!\xrightarrow{\sim}R(pq)_!$. By [def-pur-affine-space-comparison], $\gamma_{m+1}$ is $c_{p,q}^{-1}\gamma_{q,Rp^!A_Y}F_q(\gamma_m)$ after the fixed twist identification. Its transpose, written on $Rp_!Rq_!F_qT_m$, is
$$\varepsilon_{p,A_Y}\,Rp_!\bigl(\varepsilon_{q,Rp^!A_Y}\,Rq_!(\gamma_{q,Rp^!A_Y})\,Rq_!F_q(\gamma_m)\bigr).$$
This is the counit formula of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]; [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](2),(3) applies because $c_{p,q}$ was defined as the conjugate of this same $\alpha$. The inner counit and comparison give $b_{q,Rp^!A_Y}$. Naturality of $b_q$ (Step 2), applied to the map $\gamma_m$, gives
$$b_{q,Rp^!A_Y}\,Rq_!F_q(\gamma_m)=\gamma_m\,b_{q,T_m}.$$
Substitution and $I_m=\varepsilon_{p,A_Y}Rp_!(\gamma_m)$ yield the typed identity
$$I_{m+1}=I_m\,Rp_!(b_{q,T_m})\,\alpha^{-1}:V_{m+1}\longrightarrow A_Y.$$
Here $b_{q,T_m}$ has source $Rq_!T_{m+1}$ and target $T_m$; in particular no nonexistent untwisted line trace is being substituted.

source.place: Integration paragraph: the composite counit is the recursively integrated trace

proof.text:
Let $E:p^*U\xrightarrow{\sim}Rq_!r^*T$ be the canonical compact-support exchange for the base change of $a$ by $p$. The hypothesis on the specified line integrations says $p^*t_Y=t_{X_m}E$, so $t_{X_m}=p^*t_Y\,E^{-1}$. The canonical line-pullback and tensor identifications of the ordered definition are used throughout. Applying the line-transpose definition at $K=T_m$ gives
$$b_{q,T_m}=\rho_{T_m}(1_{T_m}\otimes p^*t_Y)(1_{T_m}\otimes E^{-1})\Pi^q_{T_m}.$$
Define, only as temporary maps in this proof,
$$C=Rp_!(1_{T_m}\otimes E^{-1})\,Rp_!(\Pi^q_{T_m})\,\alpha^{-1}:
V_{m+1}\longrightarrow Rp_!(T_m\otimes p^*U),$$
$$D=(\operatorname{PF}_{p,T_m,U})^{-1}C:
V_{m+1}\longrightarrow V_m\otimes U.$$
The inverses here are those justified in Step 1. Substituting the displayed expression for $b_{q,T_m}$ in Step 3 gives
$$I_{m+1}=I_m\,Rp_!\bigl(\rho_{T_m}(1_{T_m}\otimes p^*t_Y)\bigr)C.$$
This uses the assumed base-change equality only for $p:X_m\to Y$, which is among its allowed changes of base.

source.place: Integration paragraph: pull the last-coordinate line trace back from the base

proof.text:
Use naturality of the specified projection transformation [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula] for the coefficient morphism $t_Y:U\to A_Y$. Both coefficients belong to $D^b_{ctf}$, as checked in Step 1. If $P_W=\operatorname{PF}_{p,T_m,W}$, naturality is
$$Rp_!(1_{T_m}\otimes p^*t_Y)\,P_U=P_{A_Y}(1_{V_m}\otimes t_Y).$$
The unit normalization $Rp_!(\rho_{T_m})P_{A_Y}=\rho_{V_m}$ follows exactly as in Step 2 from the proper counit-defined projection map [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] and the open tensor comparison of [def-exchange-projection]. Multiply the naturality equality on the right by $P_U^{-1}C=D$ and insert it into Step 4. The result is
$$I_{m+1}=I_m\,\rho_{V_m}(1_{V_m}\otimes t_Y)D
=\rho_{A_Y}(I_m\otimes t_Y)D.$$
The last equality is just naturality of the tensor unitor and the bifunctor law for tensoring morphisms. It remains to identify this particular $D$ with the product map in the statement.

source.place: Integration paragraph: projection formula and evaluation of the recursively integrated trace

proof.text:
Apply [lem-pur-finite-forward-product-symmetry] to $(f,M)=(p,T_m)$ and $(g,N)=(a,T)$. Its bounded-below etale-origin conditions hold: the source $V_m\otimes U$ is isomorphic to the assumed bounded constructible $V_{m+1}$ by the specified $\kappa_{m,1}$; every tensor inside a compact-support functor is a bounded etale-origin complex tensored with a shifted Tate line, hence is bounded and of etale origin by [prop-weil-twist-preserves] and [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]. Exchanges identify $Rq_!r^*T$ with $p^*U$ and $Rr_!q^*T_m$ with $a^*V_m$. The canonical tensor comparisons [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] give the identifications in both forward composites. Every arrow of those composites is invertible by Step 1 and the composition comparisons [thm-sf-comp-composition]. Inverting their symmetry equality identifies their inverse products.
For $(p,a)$ that inverse is exactly the map $\kappa_{m,1}$ specified in [thm-sf-kunneth-relative]: only its displayed construction is being used, not its abstract-datum theorem. For $(a,p)$, restore the original external tensor order and the target order $V_m\otimes U$. Expanding the inverse composite then gives, in order, $\alpha^{-1}$, $Rp_!(\Pi^q_{T_m})$, $Rp_!(1_{T_m}\otimes E^{-1})$ and $P_U^{-1}$. This is $D$ from Step 4; the two symmetries in $\Pi$ are precisely the source and target symmetries in that expansion. Thus $D=\kappa_{m,1}$. Step 5 yields $I_{m+1}=(I_m\otimes t_Y)\kappa_{m,1}$ with the tensor-unit identification understood. Together with Step 2 this proves both assertions for every $m\geq1$. No coordinate-permutation invariance has been invoked.
